sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Fuquay-Varina
sections.html:
Owners here have three paths: a hired agent, a do-it-yourself sale, or a cash buyer's figure. Price trades against time and effort in each case, and the house itself usually tips the choice.

The town sits in southern Wake County, so tax value, deed filing and value appeals all run through county offices in Raleigh on any route.

  • Agent: the widest field of buyers, plus showings, repairs and a commission.
  • On your own: the commission stays with you, along with the pricing, contract and buyer screening.
  • Cash buyer: few showings and no repair list, at a figure normally below a prepared listing.

Tenants in place, an inherited house, deferred repairs or payment trouble are the cases that send owners to a cash number first.

sections.h2: A short note on the town
sections.html:
Fuquay-Varina grew from a mineral-spring resort and tobacco market into one of the faster-growing small towns in the state. Fuquay Springs incorporated in 1909 and joined Varina as one municipality in 1963. Population stood at 3,796 in 1985 and was approaching 35,000 by 2020.

Older houses near the two historic districts and newer subdivisions on the edges draw different buyers, so price each against its own comparables.

sections.h2: How Wake County values a Fuquay-Varina house
sections.html:
Wake County Tax Administration sets the value of each parcel, and the town bills from those values. The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, and the next is January 1, 2027.

After 2027 the commissioners have voted to move to a two-year cycle, with the first of those revaluations effective January 1, 2029. The county sorts its 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods and prices land and buildings from sales data. Notices of the 2027 values go out the same week the commissioners receive the results, January 19, 2027.

Search your own parcel on the county's real estate page when you pick an asking price, and ask Tax Administration which combined rate applies at your address. If a new notice looks wrong, any owner can take the value to the county's appeals board.

sections.h2: Selling with a tax bill still open
sections.html: Wake County bills fall due each September 1, and G.S. 105-360 starts interest on January 6. Taxes due in 2026 turn delinquent after January 5, 2027. If a bill is still open when you list, tell your closing attorney at once so the payoff shows up on the closing statement, and have it paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Tax break for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
Qualifying owners can get one, and the county takes the application instead of the town. The state exclusion shields half the appraised value of a permanent residence, or $25,000 if that is more, when the owner is at least 65 or disabled and earns under the state income limit.

  • The state form prints the 2026 income limit at $38,800.
  • Apply to the county assessor on Form AV-9.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion is separate and applies without an age or income test.

Only one of the three state programs can be used at a time, and Wake County posts its programs at wake.gov/taxrelief.

The town's Code Compliance Officers enforce minimum standards on overgrown grass, stored vehicles, illegal signs and trash, and the Inspections Department also enforces the town's Minimum Housing Code. An open violation can come up in a sale, so clear it before you list.

A complaint starts with a field visit within three business days. A valid complaint can bring an optional warning or a Notice of Violation, and a Resolution Agreement can set a timeline both sides accept. If nothing changes, a 72 Hour Notice of Citation follows, and the town may fine the owner or abate the problem and bill for the cost. Fines and fees left unpaid can go to the Town Board as an unpaid tax lien on the property.

The town's e-permit portal handles inspection requests, and anything requested before 3:00 pm gets a slot on the following working day.

Two statewide items sit on the seller's side of the settlement statement.

Deed excise tax, paid by the seller$1.00 on each $500 or fractional part of the valueG.S. 105-228.30

Judge each offer by the amount you keep after every cost, since the top-line figure can mislead. Put the same questions to each buyer in writing so the answers sit side by side.

  • What is the closing date, and does the contract carry a financing or inspection contingency?
  • Which side covers the excise tax, unpaid tax and the loan payoff?
  • What happens to the price if inspection finds repair needs?

If the house sits in a neighborhood with an owners association, ask the association for its resale documents early, since they can slow a closing. Cash Home Buyers can quote a Fuquay-Varina house as it now stands, and you can set that figure against a listing's net before you decide.

Start with the yard and the paper file. Both cost little to fix and either can stall a closing. A seller who walks the property with the town's standards in mind avoids a surprise notice halfway through a contract.

  • Cut overgrown grass, remove stored vehicles and haul off loose trash, the items compliance officers list first.
  • Pull your parcel record from the county and set its assessed value beside sales on nearby streets.
  • Gather the survey, repair receipts, warranty papers and, if there is an owners association, its dues and rules.
  • Check that earlier jobs, say a deck, fence or addition, had a permit and a final sign-off.

An open permit is a common surprise. Town permit staff can say which permits are on record for an address, and closing a gap before a buyer's inspector looks tends to cost less than negotiating it afterward.

Timing matters too. A house in a historic district near Main Street may draw a different buyer than a newer home in a subdivision, so ask your agent or buyer how long comparable houses sat before fixing a listing date.

sections.h2: Does the 2027 revaluation change when I should sell?
sections.html:
It can change what a buyer expects to pay in tax, though it does not change the deed. The bill due in 2027 will rest on 2027 values and on rates adopted in June 2027, while the current bill rests on 2024 values.

A seller who closes before the new notices will hand the buyer the 2024 values, and a buyer who closes after will see a fresh number on the parcel record. Neither case needs action beyond a question to Tax Administration about what it expects for your neighborhood.

For a house under contract across the new year, ask the attorney how the tax split on the settlement statement will treat the change.

faqs.q: Who sets values on Fuquay-Varina houses?
faqs.a: Wake County Tax Administration, whose next revaluation is dated January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or seller owe the deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the transferor in the statute.

faqs.q: When do Wake County tax bills go late?
faqs.a: Interest begins January 6 after a September 1 due date, under G.S. 105-360.

faqs.q: Can I list with an open town violation?
faqs.a: You can, though clearing it first avoids delay. Unpaid town fines can end up as a lien, so ask Code Compliance where yours stands.

faqs.q: Where do I file for the senior or disability tax break?
faqs.a: With the Wake County assessor on Form AV-9, which prints a 2026 income limit of $38,800.
